title: Benito Mussolini
wiki_lead:
Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini (29 July 1883 – 28 April 1945) was an Italian fascist politician who served as the prime minister of Italy from 1922 until his deposition in 1943, and then as dictator of the Italian Social Republic, a puppet state of Nazi Germany, until 1945. Known as Il Duce during his regime, he established a totalitarian dictatorship led by the National Fascist Party (PNF) in the Kingdom of Italy.
Born in Predappio, Mussolini worked as a journalist for the Italian Socialist Party (PSI) newspaper Avanti!. He was expelled from the party for advocating military intervention in World War I and called up for the Royal Italian Army in 1915, where he served until his discharge after being wounded in 1917. During the war, Mussolini turned to nationalism and denounced the PSI. He founded the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento in 1919, which opposed egalitarianism and class conflict and instead promoted a form of revolutionary nationalism transcending class lines. The Combattimento are often considered the world's first fascist movement.
The Combattimento were reorganised into the PNF in 1921. Fascist militants marched on Rome and Mussolini was appointed prime minister by King Victor Emmanuel III in 1922. He established the OVRA in 1927 to silence opposition, outlawed labour strikes, and consolidated power through the Acerbo Law among others, transforming Italy from a parliamentary democracy into a one-party state. He ordered the Pacification of Libya, characterised by some scholars as a genocide, and signed the Lateran Treaty to formally establish the Vatican City in 1929. Mussolini generally espoused autarkist and corporatist policies to grow the Italian economy, especially after the Great Depression.
Mussolini's foreign policy shifted from cautious pragmatism to expansion and alignment with Nazi Germany in the mid-1930s. He sought to expand Italy's influence without risking a major conflict with France or Britain, aligning with them during tensions over Austria. However, his invasion of Ethiopia resulted in condemnations from the League of Nations, which isolated Italy diplomatically. This pushed Mussolini toward Adolf Hitler, leading to a rapprochement and the formation of the Rome–Berlin Axis in 1936. Mussolini began militarily supporting Francisco Franco's forces during the Spanish Civil War. Although he acted as a mediator at the Munich Conference in 1938, his ambitions for territorial expansion and growing distrust of the Western powers led him to strengthen ties with Germany, resulting in the creation of the Pact of Steel in 1939.
The wars of the 1930s cost Italy enormous resources, leaving it unprepared for World War II; Mussolini declared Italy's non-belligerence. However, in June 1940, believing that German victory was imminent, he joined the war on Germany's side to share the spoils. Following defeats at the hands of the Allies and the landing in Sicily, the Grand Council of Fascism voted on the Grandi motion, which effectively ended Mussolini's leadership and restored powers to King Victor Emmanuel III who then immediately dismissed Mussolini as head of government and placed him in custody in July 1943. After the king agreed to an armistice with the Allies in September 1943, Mussolini was rescued by the Germans during the Gran Sasso raid. Hitler made Mussolini the figurehead of a puppet state in German-occupied north Italy, the Italian Social Republic, which served as a collaborationist regime of Germany. With Allied victory imminent, Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci attempted to flee to Switzerland, but were captured by communist partisans and summarily executed on 28 April 1945.

Early life

grok_lead: Benito Amilcare Andrea Mussolini (29 July 1883 â 28 April 1945) was an Italian politician, journalist, and founder of fascism who served as Prime Minister of Italy from 1922 to 1943 and, from 1925, as Duce of the National Fascist Party, establishing a one-party dictatorship. Born in Predappio to a socialist father, Mussolini initially rose as a prominent socialist editor before rejecting Marxism amid World War I, founding the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento in 1919 that evolved into the National Fascist Party. His seizure of power via the March on Rome in October 1922, amid post-war instability and strikes, prompted King Victor Emmanuel III to appoint him prime minister, after which he consolidated control through violence against opponents, electoral manipulation, and a 3 January 1925 speech to the Chamber of Deputies in which he assumed "political, moral and historical responsibility" for Fascist violence including the Matteotti murder, marking the consolidation of the dictatorship. Mussolini's regime pursued autarky, corporatism, and infrastructure projects including thousands of miles of roads, bridges, and land reclamation to boost agriculture and employment, achieving economic stabilization and reduced unemployment in the 1920s and early 1930s. Yet it suppressed dissent via Blackshirt squads, imposed racial laws in 1938, and pursued imperial expansion, notably invading Ethiopia in 1935, leading to Axis alliance with Nazi Germany and disastrous entry into World War II in 1940. Overthrown in 1943 amid military failures, he briefly headed a German puppet state before capture and execution by partisans in 1945.
